The test image shows corn plants with broad yellow-white streaking running the full length of leaves — a striking mosaic/streak pattern on young plants. Candidates: Stewart's Disease (bleached leaf streaks), Maize Dwarf Mosaic Virus (light green to yellow streaks along veins), or Maize Streak Virus.

The bold bleached streaks running the full leaf length on young plants point strongly to Stewart's Disease early phase. Let me view one reference.

The Stewart's Disease reference shows discrete, localized bleached streaks turning tan/brown — quite different from the test image.

The test image shows pervasive alternating yellow-white and green stripes running the full length of leaves on young corn plants. This is the classic pattern of Maize Streak Virus — narrow yellow-to-white stripes along the full leaf length, affecting the whole leaf surface in a clear stripe pattern parallel to veins. It differs from MDMV (which causes mosaic/mottle) and Stewart's Disease (discrete bleached spots/streaks that turn tan-brown).
